questions.default: The map in registers.map above, 32-bit word registers at 4-byte offsets starting at 0x00
questions.reason: The request names registers but gives no offsets

BUSY: offset 0x07, RO, reset 0: [0] a packet is part-way
CTR_GOOD..CTR_PROTO: offset 0x10, RO, reset 0: 0x10 good, 0x11 bad check, 0x12 short, 0x13 long, 0x14 repeat, 0x15 stale, 0x16 type or length; 16 bits, wrapping
LASTSEQ: offset 0x06, RO, reset 0: [15:0] last accepted number, [16] one once a packet was accepted

questions.text: Which byte-register format marks the end flag?
questions.default: BYTE_IN bit 8 is the END flag, bits 7:0 are the byte
questions.reason: The request says a flag but not where it sits
questions.answer: Confirmed, with one correction: the register is named BYTE (offset 0x00, RW), not BYTE_IN. Bits 7:0 hold the packet byte and bit 8 is the end flag.
questions.evidence: BYTE (0 write): bits 7:0 byte, bit 8 end flag; reads the last 9 bits written.

questions.text: Does a packet longer than expected with a length byte of 8 or less count as class 1 even when the CRC is bad?
questions.default: Yes, class 1 comes first by rule order
questions.answer: No. The proposed default is not supported. GOOD (class 1) requires a valid CRC, so a bad-CRC packet cannot be class 1. The spec's rules are listed with LONG first and GOOD last, so an over-length packet is classed LONG (4) under the first-applicable-rule requirement, and its rest is discarded to the end flag. The spec does not state the precedence between LONG and BADCRC in words; this reading relies on the listing order.
questions.evidence: LONG (4): length byte > 8, or more bytes than 4 + LEN + 4 (decided as soon as known; the rest of the packet is discarded to the end flag).
